The claimed strictly increasing trend is not supported by the paper's own data.

The paper explicitly claims, "we can notice that the fidelity score increases as the complexity of the dataset increases," but its own tables do not show a monotonic increase: Table I reports LIME fidelity as "0.4406, 0.4397, 0.4673" and Table II reports SHAP fidelity as "7.29e-18, 1.27e-17, 1.23e-17."

The paper claims 'we can notice that the fidelity score increases as the complexity of the dataset increases' on page 6, but as the reviewer points out, Table I shows LIME fidelity decreasing from 0.4406 (Dataset 1) to 0.4397 (Dataset 2), and Table II shows SHAP fidelity decreasing from 1.27e-17 (Dataset 2) to 1.23e-17 (Dataset 3).
